title: Vectors and Inner Products
summary: Column vectors in C² and C⁴, the inner product with conjugation, normalization and the computational and ± bases.
objectives: Compute the norm of a complex vector and normalize it
Compute an inner product with the conjugation on the first vector, in C² and C⁴
Build the ± basis, check orthonormality and expand a state in it
mission: The editor defines the vectors v, a, b, plus, psi, phi_plus and q. Compute norm = ‖v‖, v_hat = v/‖v‖, inner = ⟨a|b⟩, prob = |⟨a|b⟩|², minus (the vector |−⟩ in the ± basis, orthogonal to plus, normalized, with a positive first entry), amp_plus = ⟨+|ψ⟩, amp_minus = ⟨−|ψ⟩ and inner4 = ⟨φ⁺|q⟩ in C⁴.

prediction.question: For complex vectors, how are ⟨a|b⟩ and ⟨b|a⟩ related?
options: They are complex conjugates of each other
They differ by a minus sign
prediction.explanation: ⟨a|b⟩ = Σ aₖ* bₖ and ⟨b|a⟩ = Σ bₖ* aₖ. Each term of the second sum is the conjugate of the corresponding term of the first, so ⟨b|a⟩ = ⟨a|b⟩*. They are equal only when the inner product is real.

hints: The inner product ⟨a|b⟩ conjugates the entries of the first vector before multiplying. np.vdot(a, b) does exactly this, while np.dot(a, b) does not conjugate.

norm = np.linalg.norm(v) and v_hat = v / norm. For minus, flip the sign of the second entry of plus. amp_plus = np.vdot(plus, psi), and prob is the squared modulus of the inner product, abs(inner) ** 2.

norm = np.linalg.norm(v); v_hat = v / norm; inner = np.vdot(a, b); prob = abs(inner) ** 2; minus = np.array([1, -1]) / np.sqrt(2); amp_plus = np.vdot(plus, psi); amp_minus = np.vdot(minus, psi); inner4 = np.vdot(phi_plus, q).

messages.ok: All values are correct. ⟨a|b⟩ = {inner} gives probability {prob}, and |ψ⟩ has amplitudes {amp_plus} and {amp_minus} in the ± basis.
messages.not_array: The variable {name} must be an array of numbers with shape {shape}, but it holds {actual}.
messages.norm_wrong: norm should be ‖v‖ = √(Σ|vₖ|²) = {expected}, but it is {actual}. Use np.linalg.norm(v).
messages.v_hat_wrong: v_hat should be v / norm = {expected}, but it is {actual}. Divide every entry of v by its norm.
messages.inner_conjugate: inner is {actual}, the conjugate of ⟨a|b⟩. Either the conjugation is missing (np.dot) or it is applied to the second vector (np.vdot(b, a)). The conjugation belongs to the first vector: use np.vdot(a, b).
messages.inner_wrong: inner should be ⟨a|b⟩ = {expected}, but it is {actual}. Use np.vdot(a, b).
messages.prob_wrong: prob should be |⟨a|b⟩|² = {expected}, but it is {actual}. Take the squared modulus of inner with abs(inner) ** 2.
messages.minus_not_unit: minus has norm {actual}, but a basis vector must have norm 1. Divide by √2.
messages.minus_not_orthogonal: minus is not orthogonal to plus: ⟨+|−⟩ = {actual}, and it must be 0.
messages.minus_wrong: minus should be (|0⟩ − |1⟩)/√2 = {expected} (orthogonal to plus, norm 1, positive first entry), but it is {actual}.
messages.amp_plus_wrong: amp_plus should be ⟨+|ψ⟩ = {expected}, but it is {actual}. Use np.vdot(plus, psi), which conjugates plus.
messages.amp_minus_wrong: amp_minus should be ⟨−|ψ⟩ = {expected}, but it is {actual}. Use np.vdot(minus, psi).
messages.inner4_wrong: inner4 should be ⟨φ⁺|q⟩ = {expected}, but it is {actual}. The formula is the same in C⁴: np.vdot(phi_plus, q).
